bull.b: The transaction adds a differentiated oral IL-23 asset and substantial development capital, improving the combined company’s ability to fund Phase 2b and Phase 3 programs and pursue a more advanced inflammation pipeline.

A sizeable external licensing agreement provides non-dilutive validation of AVR-001’s commercial potential and could create future milestone or royalty value, although payments remain dependent on development and regulatory success.

Early clinical activity supports the potential value of the legacy oncology pipeline, while contingent rights to future monetization preserve some economic exposure for legacy shareholders after the strategic transition.

bear.b: The absence of product revenue leaves the business dependent on clinical progress, licensing, and financing rather than recurring commercial cash inflows, limiting visibility into sustainable margins and long-term earnings power.

Ongoing operating cash consumption means the company is not self-funding and will likely require external capital or transaction proceeds to sustain development, creating execution risk and potential dilution over time.

The merger materially reduces legacy shareholders’ ownership and replaces the oncology strategy with Avere’s inflammation focus. The workforce reduction may lower costs but also creates operational disruption during the transition.
